findings.evidence: The cardiothoracic ratio appears to be at the upper limits of normal or mildly enlarged on the frontal chest radiograph. The lateral view does not clearly show significant posterior displacement of the esophagus or other definitive signs of cardiomegaly.

The cardiothoracic ratio appears to be at the upper limits of normal or mildly enlarged on the frontal chest radiograph. The lateral view does not clearly show significant posterior displacement of the esophagus or other definitive signs of cardiomegaly.

verdict.limitations: The assessment of heart size on plain radiographs can be influenced by patient positioning, inspiration, and body habitus. A definitive assessment of cardiomegaly often requires echocardiography or CT imaging. Without prior imaging for comparison, it is difficult to determine if there has been a change in heart size.
